set.why: A tap is a light strike and a pound is a very forceful one; a whisper is very soft speech and a bellow is very loud speech. Speak is louder than a whisper but lacks the jump to an extreme.

why: Old why said 'bellowing is a much louder whisper', which is inaccurate (a whisper is unvoiced); restate the soft-to-extreme relation.

set.why: The usual seasonal drop could fully account for the change, so these data show no clear added effect from the campaign. That doesn’t prove hand-washing is useless; it only means these data can’t show its effect.

why: Old why overstated: said the seasonal drop 'explains' the change and the campaign 'shows no added effect'; the data only fail to show an effect.

set.why: Sales rose even more in the rest of the city, so Main Street’s rise likely reflects a citywide trend and can’t be credited to the ban. Saying the ban caused a precise 3% loss treats a rough comparison as exact proof.

why: Clarify reasoning: the point is that a citywide trend, not the ban, may explain the rise; matches the hedged wording of the correct option.

set.q: Four friends sit in a row of four seats. All directions are from the viewpoint of someone facing the row. Farah sits in the far-left seat. Dev is not in an end seat. Elif sits immediately to Dev’s right. Gus does not sit next to Elif. Where does Gus sit?

why: Removes left/right perspective ambiguity: if 'Dev’s right' were read from Dev’s own seated viewpoint (facing the viewer), Elif would be in seat 2 and Gus far-right, giving a second defensible answer.
